reader_summary.overview: I'm your host, Eddie Palmyan, and next to me in the studio is my friend and colleague, Niklas Savos. It's really hot in Sweden, I couldn't sleep, but otherwise fine. And today we have the honor of speaking with a legendary investor and author, Will Thorndyke.

key_points.text: He founded the private equity firm Hussatonic Partners in 1994, which has since grown to more than $1 billion in AUM.

key_points.text: And he is also currently running compounding labs, and the hedge fund, Sun Mountain Partners, and the new podcast, 50X.

thesis: This episode argues that investors should distinguish between companies successfully shifting capital allocation toward share buybacks to create value (like Microsoft) and those where the outcome remains uncertain (like Cisco). It also highlights the importance of long-term holding companies such as Constellation and Brookfield, while noting that some firms are actively processing ideas from the book to improve their unit economics and share repurchase strategies.
